correctness.rationale: Using the Fano-plane incidence rule point i meets line j iff i-j mod7 lies in {0,1,3}, independently enumerated all C(14,5)=2002 five-sets; exactly 1750 induce a disconnected subgraph and their nine-vertex complements define facets of ordinary Delta_5(H). Full downward closure contains 14633 augmented simplices, nonempty dimension counts (14,91,364,1001,2002,3003,3432,2975,1750). Element-matching rounds through fourteen vertices give 7071 valid disjoint face-coface matches including the empty face; independently topologically sorting all 14633 vertices of the oriented Hasse diagram proves acyclicity. After unaugmenting, the Morse CW complex has one critical 0-cell and 491 critical 8-cells, so its integral homotopy type is wedge491 S8, not merely a rational rank. Independent Fano incidence automorphism enumeration gives |Aut(H)|=336, and signed fixed-simplex Lefschetz sums yield the eight type/count/trace triples (1,- identity 491), (1^6 2^4;21,-29), (1^2 2^2 4^2;42,-1), (1^2 3^4;56,5), (2^7;28,-11), (2,4,8;84,1), (2,6,6;56,1),(7,7;48,1). Their weighted trace average is zero; finite-group rational transfer proves reduced rational quotient homology vanishes, not quotient contractibility. All these finite configurations were exhaustively recreated by independent code.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the canonical smallest finite projective-plane incidence graph, with a substantial intrinsic 336-element symmetry group. An explicit complete integral wedge classification of its ordinary five-cut complex plus the full automorphism character and rational quotient acyclicity supplies a natural, reusable sharp finite benchmark beyond merely counting faces. The high-girth generic criterion does not apply, so the exact configuration genuinely needs separate reasoning.
